26-sf1-qb-1767.solution: An inflection point is where the second derivative changes sign, so set it equal to 0. The first derivative is 3x² − 12x and the second is 6x − 12, which is 0 when x = 2. Then f(2) = 2³ − 6 × 2² = 8 − 24 = −16. The inflection point is (2, −16).
26-sf1-qb-1767.trick: For a cubic ax³ + bx² + cx + d, the inflection is at x = −b ÷ (3a) = 6 ÷ 3 = 2. Only one option has x = 2, so you can stop there.

26-sf1-qb-1777.solution: The false positive rate is the share of healthy people who test positive. So the expected number is 1% of 1,000 = 0.01 × 1,000 = 10. The answer is 10 people.
26-sf1-qb-1777.trick: 1% is one in every hundred, so just do 1,000 ÷ 100 = 10.

26-sf1-qb-1781.solution: After n half-lives the mass left is (1/2)ⁿ of the original. 1/8 = (1/2)³, so 3 half-lives passed in 48 hours. One half-life is 48 ÷ 3 = 16 hours.
26-sf1-qb-1781.trick: 1/8 means halving three times (2 × 2 × 2 = 8). Split 48 hours into 3 equal parts: 16.

26-sf1-qb-1795.solution: A ratio of 1:12 means the real size is 12 times the model size. The real part is 0.5 × 12 = 6 m. So the answer is 6 m.

26-sf1-qb-1805.solution: East and north are at right angles, so the displacement is the hypotenuse. d = √(15² + 20²) = √(225 + 400) = √625 = 25 km. The displacement is 25 km.
26-sf1-qb-1805.trick: 15 and 20 are 5 × 3 and 5 × 4, so this is the 3, 4, 5 triangle times 5. The hypotenuse is 5 × 5 = 25.

26-sf1-qb-1813.solution: The integers from 1 to 50 are 50 numbers in all. The multiples of 7 are 7, 14, 21, 28, 35, 42 and 49, which is 7 numbers. So the probability is 7/50.
26-sf1-qb-1813.trick: 50 ÷ 7 is 7 and a bit, so there are 7 multiples out of 50 numbers: 7/50.

26-sf1-qb-1819.solution: Strength scales with area, and area scales with the square of the length ratio. The area factor is 50² = 2,500. So the real bridge can resist 200 × 2,500 = 500,000 N.
26-sf1-qb-1819.trick: Length 50 times bigger means area 50 × 50 = 2,500 times bigger. For 200 × 2,500, do 2 × 25 = 50 and add four zeros: 500,000. The other options are only 25 and 250 times bigger.

26-sf1-qb-1824.solution: In a square, the diagonal splits the 90° corner into two equal angles. As a check, tan θ = 40 ÷ 40 = 1, so θ = 45°. The angle is 45°.
26-sf1-qb-1824.trick: The diagonal cuts the right angle in half, so 90° ÷ 2 = 45°. The 40 m does not matter.

26-sf1-bm-2450.solution: The determinant of a matrix equals the product of its eigenvalues. So det = 5 × (−1) = −5. The determinant is −5.
26-sf1-bm-2450.trick: Determinant is the product of the eigenvalues (the sum would be the trace). 5 × −1 = −5.

26-sf1-bm-2455.solution: Take the distance along the ground from the foot of the tower, since the question does not say. The angle of depression at the top equals the angle of elevation from the car, so tan 45° = 80 ÷ d. As tan 45° = 1, d = 80 m. The car is 80 m away.
26-sf1-bm-2455.trick: At 45° the two shorter sides of the right triangle are equal, so the distance equals the height: 80.
26-sf1-bm-2455.computed: 80 m (along the ground; 80√2 ≈ 113 m along the line of sight)
26-sf1-bm-2455.comment: The question does not say what the distance is measured from. Along the ground from the foot of the tower it is 80 m, which is the show's answer, but from the top of the tower along the line of sight it would be 80√2 ≈ 113 m.

26-sf1-bm-2459.solution: Relative error = absolute error ÷ measured value = 0.5 ÷ 400 = 0.00125. As a percentage that is 0.00125 × 100 = 0.125%. The relative error is 0.125%.
26-sf1-bm-2459.trick: 1% of 400 is 4, and 0.5 is one eighth of 4, so the error is one eighth of 1%, which is 0.125%. It must be under 1%, which rules out 12.5% and 1.25%.

26-sf1-bm-2465.trick: 36 × 36 = 1,296, so 3,600² ÷ 1,000 = 12,960. Times 10 gives 129,600. The digits must be 1296, and only one option has them.

26-sf1-bm-2475.solution: Energy = power × time = 75,000 W × 3,600 s = 270,000,000 J. Divide by 1,000,000 to get megajoules. So the energy is 270 MJ.
26-sf1-bm-2475.trick: 75 kW for one hour is 75 kWh, and 1 kWh = 3.6 MJ. So 75 × 3.6 = 270 (75 × 3 = 225, plus 75 × 0.6 = 45).

26-sf1-bm-2481.solution: The modulus of a + bi is √(a² + b²). So |z| = √(11² + 60²) = √(121 + 3,600) = √3,721 = 61. The modulus is 61.
26-sf1-bm-2481.trick: Know the triple 11, 60, 61. Test it: (11² − 1) ÷ 2 = 120 ÷ 2 = 60, which matches the 60 given. When that matches, the hypotenuse is one more than the longer leg: 61.

26-sf1-bm-2484.solution: The rocket is on the ground when h(t) = 0. −5t² + 100t = −5t(t − 20) = 0, so t = 0 (the launch) or t = 20. It hits the ground at t = 20 s.
26-sf1-bm-2484.trick: For h = −at² + bt, the landing time is b ÷ a. Here 100 ÷ 5 = 20.

26-sf1-bm-2487.solution: The amount of drug does not change when diluting, so C₁V₁ = C₂V₂. 40 × V₁ = 10 × 100, so V₁ = 1,000 ÷ 40 = 25 mL. The initial volume was 25 mL.
26-sf1-bm-2487.trick: The concentration drops by a factor of 4 (40 to 10), so the starting volume is a quarter of the final: 100 ÷ 4 = 25.

26-sf1-bm-2492.solution: By the power rule, y = 5x³ gives dy/dx = 5 × 3x² = 15x². At x = 1 this is 15 × 1² = 15. The derivative at x = 1 is 15.
26-sf1-bm-2492.trick: At x = 1, every power of x is 1, so the derivative is just coefficient × power: 5 × 3 = 15.

26-sf1-bm-2495.solution: Differentiate term by term: 2x² gives 4x and 4x gives 4, so dy/dx = 4x + 4. At x = 1 that is 4 + 4 = 8. So dy/dx = 8.
26-sf1-bm-2495.trick: At x = 1, each term gives coefficient × power: 2 × 2 = 4 and 4 × 1 = 4. Add them to get 8.

26-sf1-bm-2500.solution: This is a binomial with n = 4, p = 0.7 and 3 successes. P = C(4, 3) × 0.7³ × 0.3 = 4 × 0.343 × 0.3 = 0.4116. The probability is about 0.41.

26-sf1-bm-2505.solution: From 320 mCi to 40 mCi is a drop by a factor of 320 ÷ 40 = 8 = 2³. So 3 half-lives passed in 18 hours. One half-life is 18 ÷ 3 = 6 hours.
26-sf1-bm-2505.trick: 320, 160, 80, 40 is three halvings. Split 18 hours into 3 equal parts: 6.

26-sf1-bm-2509.solution: Percentage yield = actual ÷ theoretical × 100, so actual = 70% of 2,400 = 0.7 × 2,400 = 1,680 g. The actual yield is 1,680 g.

26-sf1-bm-2515.solution: Marginal cost is the derivative of the cost function: dC/dx = 6x² − 8x. At x = 2 that is 6 × 4 − 8 × 2 = 24 − 16 = 8. The marginal cost is 8.
26-sf1-bm-2515.trick: The constant 10 disappears. Write the derivative as 2x(3x − 4), which at x = 2 is 4 × 2 = 8.

26-sf1-bm-2521.solution: Newton-Raphson gives x₁ = x₀ − f(x₀) ÷ f′(x₀), with f(x) = x² − 4 and f′(x) = 2x. So x₁ = 2.5 − (6.25 − 4) ÷ 5 = 2.5 − 0.45 = 2.05. The next approximation is 2.05.
26-sf1-bm-2521.trick: For x² − a, Newton's step is the average of x₀ and a ÷ x₀. Here 4 ÷ 2.5 = 1.6, and the average of 2.5 and 1.6 is 2.05.

26-sf1-bm-2526.solution: Acceleration is the derivative of velocity: a = dv/dt = 3t² − 6. At t = 2 that is 3 × 4 − 6 = 12 − 6 = 6. The acceleration is 6 m/s².
26-sf1-bm-2526.trick: 3t² at t = 2 is 12, and the −6t term leaves −6. So 12 − 6 = 6.

26-sf1-bm-2532.solution: Rate in the whole container = 0.05 mol/L/s × 5 L = 0.25 mol/s. Time for 2 mol = 2 ÷ 0.25 = 8 s. The time is 8 seconds.
26-sf1-bm-2532.trick: 0.25 mol per second is one mole every 4 seconds, so 2 moles take 8 seconds.

26-sf1-bm-2536.solution: Vertical component = magnitude × sin θ, with θ measured from the horizontal axis. So it is 25 × sin 90° = 25 × 1 = 25. The vertical component is 25.
26-sf1-bm-2536.trick: 90° points straight up, so the whole vector is vertical: 25. The 0 option is the horizontal part, 25 cos 90°.

26-sf1-bm-2543.solution: North and east are at right angles, so the distance is the hypotenuse. d = √(300² + 400²) = √(90,000 + 160,000) = √250,000 = 500 km. The distance from the start is 500 km.
26-sf1-bm-2543.trick: 300 and 400 are 100 times 3 and 4, so this is the 3, 4, 5 triangle times 100: 500.

26-sf1-bm-2547.trick: The minus sign does not matter because it gets squared. 5 and 12 make the 5, 12, 13 triangle, so 13.

26-sf1-bm-2550.solution: The angle of depression from the cliff top equals the angle of elevation from the boat, so tan 30° = 50 ÷ d. So d = 50 ÷ tan 30° = 50 ÷ (1/√3) = 50√3, which is about 86.6 m. The boat is 50√3 m from the base.
26-sf1-bm-2550.trick: tan 30° = 1/√3, so dividing by it just multiplies by √3: 50√3. The boat must be farther than 50 m (that is the 45° case), so the 50 m option is out.

26-sf1-bm-2554.solution: An inflexion point is where the second derivative changes sign, so set it equal to 0. R′(t) = 6t² − 18t + 12, so R″(t) = 12t − 18. Setting 12t − 18 = 0 gives t = 18 ÷ 12 = 1.5. The inflexion point is at t = 1.5.
26-sf1-bm-2554.trick: For a cubic with terms at³ + bt², the inflexion is at t = −b ÷ (3a) = 9 ÷ 6 = 1.5.

26-sf1-bm-2558.solution: The ratio 1 : 4 : 5 has 1 + 4 + 5 = 10 parts. Sand is 4 of the 10 parts, so its mass is 4/10 × 4,500 = 1,800 kg. The mass of sand is 1,800 kg.
26-sf1-bm-2558.trick: 10 parts means each part is 450 kg. Sand is 4 parts, so 4 × 450 = 1,800.

26-sf1-bm-2566.trick: Going from kg/m³ to g/cm³ always divides by 1,000 (water is 1,000 kg/m³ and 1 g/cm³). 11,300 ÷ 1,000 = 11.3.

26-sf1-bm-2572.solution: Newton-Raphson gives x₁ = x₀ − f(x₀) ÷ f′(x₀), with f(x) = x² − 4 and f′(x) = 2x. So x₁ = 3 − (9 − 4) ÷ 6 = 3 − 5/6 = 13/6. The value of x₁ is 13/6.
26-sf1-bm-2572.trick: For x² − a, average x₀ and a ÷ x₀: (3 + 4/3) ÷ 2 = (13/3) ÷ 2 = 13/6. Also x₁ must be between 2 and 3, and only 13/6 is.

26-sf1-bm-2787.solution: z = (value − mean) ÷ SD = (25 − 30) ÷ 5 = −5 ÷ 5 = −1. The minus sign means below the mean, so the commute is 1 SD below. The answer is −1.
26-sf1-bm-2787.trick: 25 is 5 below 30, and one SD is 5, so it is exactly 1 SD below: −1.

26-sf1-bm-2792.solution: z = (sample mean − population mean) ÷ (SD ÷ √n). The standard error is 4 ÷ √16 = 4 ÷ 4 = 1. So z = (52 − 50) ÷ 1 = 2. The z-score is 2.
26-sf1-bm-2792.trick: √16 = 4 cancels the SD of 4, so the standard error is 1. Then z is just the difference in means: 52 − 50 = 2.

26-sf1-bm-2797.solution: Each of the 7 elements is either in a subset or out, so there are 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 = 2⁷ subsets. 2⁷ = 128. The number of subsets is 128.
26-sf1-bm-2797.trick: Double seven times: 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128. The other options are 2⁶ = 64 and 2⁸ = 256.

26-sf1-bm-2800.solution: Range = largest value − smallest value = 90 − 45 = 45. The range is 45.
26-sf1-bm-2800.trick: The list is already in order, so just subtract the two ends: 90 − 45 = 45.

26-sf1-bm-2804.solution: There are 7 values, so the median is the 4th value, 10. With the median left out, the top three values are 12, 14 and 16, and the middle of those is 14. So Q3 is 14.
26-sf1-bm-2804.trick: With 7 values, Q3 is the 6th value (the middle of the top three). Count along: 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14 and stop.

26-sf1-bm-2808.solution: z = (score − mean) ÷ SD = (85 − 75) ÷ 5 = 10 ÷ 5 = 2. Her score is 2 SD above the mean.
26-sf1-bm-2808.trick: 85 is 10 above 75, and 10 is two lots of 5, so 2 SDs.

26-sf1-bm-2811.solution: A year has about 52 weeks, so 4 years has 4 × 52 = 208 weeks. As a check, 4 × 365 = 1,460 days and 1,460 ÷ 7 ≈ 208.6, which is 208 full weeks. The answer is 208 weeks.
26-sf1-bm-2811.trick: 4 × 50 = 200 and 4 × 2 = 8, so 208. The other options are far off.

26-sf1-bm-2815.solution: In a basic boxplot the box runs from Q1 to Q3, and the whiskers reach out from the box to the smallest and largest values. Q1 and Q3 are the ends of the box, not the whiskers, and mean ± SD is not drawn at all. If outliers are plotted separately, the whiskers stop at the most extreme values that are not outliers. So the answer is Minimum and maximum values.
26-sf1-bm-2815.trick: Q1 and Q3 are the box edges and a boxplot never uses mean ± SD, so only the minimum and maximum are left.

26-sf1-bm-2820.solution: Each phone is chosen with probability 1/2. P(good) = 1/2 × 0.7 + 1/2 × 0.8 = 0.35 + 0.40 = 0.75. The probability is 0.75.
26-sf1-bm-2820.trick: Equal chances means take the average of 0.7 and 0.8, which is halfway between them: 0.75.

26-sf1-bm-2827.solution: Simple interest = P × R × T ÷ 100 = 5,000 × 8 × 5 ÷ 100 = ₦2,000. The simple interest is ₦2,000.
26-sf1-bm-2827.trick: 8% a year for 5 years is 40% of the principal, and 40% of 5,000 is 2,000.

26-sf1-bm-2831.solution: Percentage = part ÷ whole × 100 = 12 ÷ 40 × 100 = 0.3 × 100 = 30%. So 30% of the class are girls.
26-sf1-bm-2831.trick: 10% of 40 is 4, and 12 is three lots of 4, so 30%.

26-sf1-bm-2836.solution: Any 3 of the 20 points make a triangle, unless all 3 come from the 5 collinear points. The number of triples is C(20, 3) = 20 × 19 × 18 ÷ 6 = 1,140. The 5 collinear points give C(5, 3) = 10 triples that are not triangles. So the number of triangles is 1,140 − 10 = 1,130.
26-sf1-bm-2836.trick: 20 × 19 × 3 = 1,140, then take away 10 to get 1,130. The answer cannot be above 1,140, which rules out 3,310 and 1,210.

26-sf1-bm-2842.solution: Put the times in order: 4, 5, 6, 8, 9. There are 5 values, so the median is the middle one, the 3rd, which is 6. The median response time is 6 seconds.
26-sf1-bm-2842.trick: Sort first, because the middle of the unsorted list is 4. The 3rd smallest is 6.

26-sf1-bm-2847.solution: There are 36 outcomes, and 25 have no 4, so 36 − 25 = 11 outcomes have at least one 4. Of these, only (4, 4) has a sum of 8. So the probability is 1/11.
26-sf1-bm-2847.trick: Outcomes with a 4: 6 + 6 − 1 = 11. Only the double 4 makes 8, so 1 out of 11.

26-sf1-bm-2854.solution: Quartile deviation = (Q3 − Q1) ÷ 2, which is half the interquartile range. So the IQR = 2 × 4 = 8. The interquartile range is 8.
26-sf1-bm-2854.trick: Quartile deviation is half the IQR, so just double it: 4 × 2 = 8.

26-sf1-bm-2860.solution: Permutations of n objects taken r at a time: P(n, r) = n! ÷ (n − r)!. So P(7, 3) = 7! ÷ 4! = 7 × 6 × 5 = 210. The number of permutations is 210.
26-sf1-bm-2860.trick: Multiply three numbers counting down from 7: 7 × 6 × 5 = 42 × 5 = 210. The other options are 7! = 5,040 and the combinations C(7, 3) = 35.

26-sf1-bm-2867.solution: The standard deviation measures how far the values spread from the mean. If every value is 15, the mean is 15 and every deviation from it is 0. So the variance and the standard deviation are both 0. The answer is 0.
26-sf1-bm-2867.trick: No spread at all means 0. Every value equals the mean, so there is nothing to measure.
26-sf1-bm-2867.comment: The answer is right, but the third option is printed as the letter O, which looks like a scan slip for the digit 0. The option text should be changed to 0 so it matches the show's answer.

26-sf1-bm-2871.solution: A parameter is a fixed value that describes a whole population, and it is usually unknown. A statistic describes a sample, an estimator is a rule that uses sample data to estimate a parameter, and a predictor is an input variable in a model. So the answer is Parameter.
26-sf1-bm-2871.trick: Parameter goes with Population (both start with P), while a statistic goes with a sample.

26-sf1-bm-2875.solution: P(at least one) = 1 − P(none). P(none) = 0.9 × 0.9 × 0.9 = 0.729. So P(at least one) = 1 − 0.729 = 0.271.
26-sf1-bm-2875.trick: Use the opposite: 0.9 × 0.9 = 0.81, then 0.81 × 0.9 = 0.729, and 1 − 0.729 = 0.271. It cannot be more than 3 × 0.1 = 0.3, so 0.334 is out.

26-sf1-bm-2879.solution: A long left tail means the distribution is negatively skewed. The few very small values pull the mean down towards the tail, while the median stays near the bulk of the data. So the mean is below the median: Mean < Median.
26-sf1-bm-2879.trick: The mean is dragged towards the long tail. The tail is on the left, so the mean sits to the left of the median: mean < median.
accept: mean is less than the median

26-sf1-bm-2885.solution: Range = highest − lowest = 300 − 150 = 150. The range is $150K.
26-sf1-bm-2885.trick: Spot the biggest (300) and the smallest (150) and subtract. The order of the list does not matter.

26-sf1-bm-2894.solution: There are 4 aces and 13 hearts, but the ace of hearts is counted in both. So there are 4 + 13 − 1 = 16 cards that are an ace or a heart. P = 16/52 = 4/13.
26-sf1-bm-2894.trick: 16 cards out of 52. Divide top and bottom by 4: 4/13.

26-sf1-bm-2898.solution: Put the numbers in order: 10, 12, 15, 20, 25, 30. There are 6 values, so the median is the mean of the 3rd and 4th: (15 + 20) ÷ 2 = 17.5. The median is 17.5 eggs.
26-sf1-bm-2898.trick: With an even count, sort and take the middle pair, 15 and 20, then go halfway: 17.5.

26-sf1-bm-2903.solution: Put 1 ball in each box first, which leaves 12 − 5 = 7 balls to place freely in 5 boxes. By stars and bars the count is C(7 + 5 − 1, 5 − 1) = C(11, 4) = 11 × 10 × 9 × 8 ÷ 24 = 330. The answer is 330.
26-sf1-bm-2903.trick: Use C(11, 4) and cancel early: 8 ÷ 4 = 2, 9 ÷ 3 = 3, 10 ÷ 2 = 5, leaving 11 × 5 × 3 × 2 = 330. The 1,820 option is for boxes that may be empty, so it is out.
